model: lucidrains segformer-pytorch Segformer (MiT-b0-like dims 32/64/160/256, from scratch), 1-ch input, saturated-pixel zeroing + pointwise norm_log, PixelShuffle(4) full-res head + residual conv refine, BCE(pos_weight 5)+dice; fine-tuned from lseg_b; flip TTA at test

eval.threshold_from: val sweep (--val-thr) with flip TTA, every 4th val image

notes: Run lseg_d (round 2): seg.train --init-ckpt lseg_b best.pt (step 6000), --set model.norm=pointwise train.lr=3e-4 train.warmup=200 loss.pos_weight=5.0, 64.7 min on 1 L40S (sdfada013 idx3), 10238 steps; best.pt = step 9000 (val F1 0.898 on 200 val imgs, thr 0.995). Total training incl. lseg_b init: 71.3 + 64.7 min. Test threshold 0.998 picked on VAL (every 2nd val image, val peak F1 0.904); Reported eval: same lseg_d best.pt with flip TTA (mean of 4 flips), threshold 0.98 picked on VAL with TTA (every 4th val image, val F1 0.907); whole test 1529 imgs, tiled 1024: peak F1 0.8998. Without TTA (thr .998 from val, val F1 .904): test peak F1 0.8966 (kept under eval.no_tta_same_ckpt). Round 1 (lseg_b, per-image standardisation, landed earlier): test peak F1 0.8255, pixel IoU 0.410. What helped: (1) PixelShuffle(4) full-res head (Segformer decodes at 1/4 res, peaks are 1-2 px); (2) zeroing saturated >=60000 pixels (lseg_a val P 0.10 from 65535 panel-edge lines); (3) pointwise norm_log instead of per-image standardisation, which keeps absolute brightness (val F1 .809 -> .898). Dead end: BCE pos_weight 10 -> 2 alone (lseg_c) did not fix precision.
